item: Reconciled cash statement and valuation driver schedule
period: At 27 November 2026 and monthly over the forecast
why: The packet does not establish unrestricted cash, affordable reinvestment or a defensible forecast.
conclusion: The date Juniper needs funding and the cash flows available for valuation.
action: Reconcile the cash balance and forecast drivers, and retest method eligibility.

item: Dated like-for-like subscription offers and tier terms
period: Both offers in force at 27 November 2026
why: Recorded pricing disagrees and the copied release is one origin.
conclusion: Whether USD 40 and USD 55 are comparable entry prices for the same contract.
action: Align dates and included features before using pricing in comparables.

item: Signed customer agreements, software IP assignments and issued-share register
why: The registry names the company but identifies none of these rights.
conclusion: Which entity owns the operating assets, earns the contract receipts and issues the shares.
action: Match each agreement and assignment to the registered entity and reconcile the securities.

item: Subscription terms, invoice lines and credits for the two paying accounts
period: The reported year and each contract’s current term
why: Annual recognised sales combine charges with unknown recurrence.
conclusion: How much contracted revenue can enter the valuation and which sales have been collected or renewed.
action: Tie recurring charges to enforceable terms, separate one-time items, and reconcile receipts and direct costs.

item: Dated comparable transaction prices and matched company revenue
why: Subscription list prices measure what users pay. They do not establish the enterprise price paid for a business.
conclusion: Whether a revenue multiple can support an enterprise valuation.
action: Match enterprise value and revenue period, accounting and business mix before calculating a multiple.

item: Dated customer cohorts and churn reconciliation
period: From each account’s first invoice through its latest renewal opportunity
why: The ledger does not describe renewals or switching.
conclusion: Whether customers renew and how much growth must come from acquiring new accounts.
action: Test retention and switching behaviour by customer vintage.
